newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas firms on stock refills, outages.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas firms on stock refills, outages.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices were steady to higher Thursday as buyers continued to inject gas into storage and an Alabama gas plant remained out of service, industry sources said.
Prices at the Henry Hub, La., on average were up one cent from Wednesday at $2.19-2.20 early and $2.23-2.24 late, while Transco (Station 65) was quoted mostly in the low-$2.20s.
Contributing to the late arrival of buyers was the uptick in the futures market, traders said. NYMEX June Henry Hub natgas jumped to a high of $2.25, up 4.4 cents, by 1350 EDT.
The absence of some capacity in the Gulf as a result of Mobil Corp's maintenance outage has left buyers relying on Texas and Midwest supplies.
Maintenance at Mobil's Mary Ann gas plant in Coden, Ala., is expected to last until mid-June. Total capacity of the plant is 380-390 mmcfd, and about 120 mmcfd is due back early next week.
However, Transco is expected to fully restore its Texas gas line Friday, which will return about 600 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) to the market.
South Texas prices also gained one cent to about $2.11-2.12, while west Texas prices in the Permian basin were about one cent lower at $1.95-1.98.

Contributing to the pressure was news that Southern California Gas Co was declaring an overnomination day this Saturday due to excess supplies at the delivery point. The company asked its shippers to trim nominations to no more than 110 percent of their anticipated usage.
Also, Pacific Gas and Electric said its 1,087 Diablo Canyon 1 nuclear unit will likely reconnect to the grid next Thursday after shutting down April 19 for refueling.

In the East, where plant outages are keeping the market tight, New York city-gate prices remained in the mid-$2.40s, while Appalachian prices were bumped up about one cent in response to the firmer Gulf cash to about $2.38-2.39 on Columbia.
In the Midcontinent, prices remained just over $2 as buyers continued to pump gas into storage, market sources said.

Forecasts in the Midcontinent are calling for more moderate temperatures over the weekend but then a return of cooler air by early next week. In Chicago, temperature highs are expected to reach 77 degrees F on Friday, 74 on Saturday and 68 on Sunday, according to Weather Services Corp.
